flawed_step: Step 2: Inferring that k = ceil(n/2) guarantees every shorter tour differs from the current tour in at most k edges, or guarantees an improving intermediate k-change. Two tours can be edge-disjoint and hence differ in all n edges; a sequence ending at a shorter tour need not contain an improving move from the original tour.
assessment_summary: The direct proof works only when the current tour and a shorter tour share at least floor(n/2) edges. It cannot handle edge-disjoint tours. More decisively, edge-disjoint tours can be adjacent vertices of the symmetric TSP polytope. An exposing linear edge-cost vector can make one such tour globally optimal and the other better than every remaining tour. After adding a common constant to every edge cost, all weights are nonnegative without changing tour comparisons. The second tour is then a ceil(n/2)-Opt local optimum but is not globally optimal.
